When the arms are held up without support, neck and shoulder muscles keep working, and fatigue builds over the day, especially in the same position on the same side.

Quinn's first golf day in six months: three buckets, 300 swings, no warm-up. Next morning, back, elbow and shoulder all had opinions.

The golf swing is a fast twist repeated around a hundred times a round. If the hips and mid-back are stiff, the low back often takes up the slack, and a sudden jump in practice after a week at a desk adds to it.

Tips that may help: a ten-minute dynamic warm-up starting with short irons, daily hip and mid-back rotation, strength training twice a week, and building practice gradually with an easy grip, fitted clubs and a push cart.

Pain that lingers or gets worse, or any numbness or weakness, is worth getting checked. Easing off a sore elbow early is wise.
